name: syndrome locates a single error
mechanism: add check bits so that every single-bit error produces a distinct pattern of failed checks; the receiver recomputes the checks and the pattern of failures is the position of the flipped bit, which is then corrected

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Hamming(7,4)' in section Information theory and signal processing / Coding theory / Error detection and correction: a Hamming code that encodes 4 bits of data into 7 bits by adding 3 parity bits

requires: a check matrix whose columns are distinct and nonzero
fails_when: two errors decode to a wrong position
rate cost of the check bits
